defects.justification: Dependency "@aws-sdk/client-s3": "^3.750.0" uses a caret range, so installs can silently pull newer minor/patch releases; there is no lockfile in the app to pin the resolved version.
Dependency "@aws-sdk/lib-storage": "^3.750.0" uses a caret range, so installs can silently pull newer minor/patch releases; there is no lockfile in the app to pin the resolved version.
Dependency "croner": "^9.0.0" uses a caret range, so installs can silently pull newer minor/patch releases; there is no lockfile in the app to pin the resolved version.
Dependency "tar": "^7.4.3" uses a caret range, so installs can silently pull newer minor/patch releases; there is no lockfile in the app to pin the resolved version.
Dependency "@types/node": "^22.10.0" uses a caret range, so installs can silently pull newer minor/patch releases; there is no lockfile in the app to pin the resolved version.
Dependency "typescript": "^5.7.0" uses a caret range, so installs can silently pull newer minor/patch releases; there is no lockfile in the app to pin the resolved version.
Dependency "vitest": "^3.0.0" uses a caret range, so installs can silently pull newer minor/patch releases; there is no lockfile in the app to pin the resolved version.

tar is created with portable: true, which omits uid/gid/uname/gname from entries; restoring a system backup (e.g. /etc, /var/www as in config.example.json) with tar -C / leaves files owned by the restoring user, so the backup cannot faithfully restore the directories.

The S3Client is created without any request/connection timeout, so a hung upload or list call never completes; because BackupRunner skips runs while one is in progress, a single stalled request silently stops all future backups.

All tests use the in-memory MemoryStore; S3Store (multipart upload, paginated ListObjectsV2 with continuation tokens, delete) and createS3Store are never exercised, so the real upload/retention path is untested.
